cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: What Are We Now?
cards.instruction: Find out how someone defines the relationship without directly asking for a label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I approve another overnight visit, tell me which towel I'm using.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Local supply approved. The guest towel, or the one that's always been mine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours is still on the hook. Are you inspecting my bathroom now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm settling the arrangements. Do you want my towel back on its hook after I leave, or are you requesting its transfer to the guest laundry?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 conditions visit approval on arrangements, A3 approves supply while probing personal status and A5 recasts future towel placement as B request, sustaining superior form around an indirect belonging question.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 available towel prompts A3 guest/personal distinction; B4 unchanged hook and inspection challenge prompt A5 active future-placement test.

relationship.evidence: B2 is hospitable and B4 notices A controlling manner while supplying the needed fact, responding to both cards.

heightening.evidence: B4 mere unchanged location could be inertia, so A5 asks what B wants after the visit, a more revealing choice.

specificity.evidence: A1 overnight visit and A3 formerly personal towel establish a real private arrangement; A5 now keeps person and object references literal.
